newsitem.title: USA: UAL's United asks US, Japan to OK air applications.
newsitem.headline: UAL's United asks US, Japan to OK air applications.

text.p: UAL Corp's United Airlines on Wednesday encouraged U.S. and Japanese transportation authorities to approve pending applications for air service.

In a Department of Transportion filing, the airline urged the department to approve applications for Japan Airlines to switch designations for its Tokyo to Atlanta and Tokyo to Kona, Hawaii, services, allowing it to increase its weekly flights to Kona from three to seven.

United said the U.S. approval of these adjustments should "be based on an understanding that the Japanese government will reciprocate by granting routine approval to service adjustments by U.S. air carriers."
This includes United's service increase on the route from New York's John F. Kennedy airport to Tokyo and its current second daily flight between Los Angeles and Tokyo, it added.
"Mutual approval of these services should help to set the stage for sucessful bilateral negotiations on other pending issues," United said.
